title: FedPRE: Robust Federated Graph Learning against Topological Corruption

problem.claim: Federated Graph Learning suffers from real-world data corruption, including topological corruption that disrupts graph connectivity patterns and causes flawed feature propagation by GNNs.

gap.claim: Existing Federated Learning and Federated Graph Learning studies have addressed label corruption, but graph topological corruption remains unexamined and lacks targeted strategies for global contaminated collaboration and local vulnerability.

contributions.claim: FedPRE is proposed to improve the robustness of Federated Graph Learning against topological corruption.
Feature Propagation Robustness Evaluation evaluates client GNN feature-propagation robustness and adjusts client contributions during aggregation.
Topological Corruption-Resistant Enhancement improves robustness against corruption during local training.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments validate FedPRE's robustness and effectiveness against topological corruption.
The authors report that the code is available in a public GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Federated Graph Learning is presented as a privacy-preserving paradigm for distributed GNN training.
Real-world data corruption affects Federated Graph Learning, with topological corruption disrupting connectivity and feature propagation.
Prior work addressed label corruption but did not examine topological corruption or provide targeted robustness strategies.
The paper proposes FedPRE, combining client robustness evaluation during aggregation with corruption-resistant local enhancement.
The authors report extensive experimental validation and code availability.

source_observation.claim: Topological corruption can cause GNNs to learn flawed feature-propagation patterns by disrupting node connectivity.

interpretation.claim: Robust graph learning may need to evaluate and control the reliability of structural information used for propagation.

application.claim: In federated graph systems, consider combining robustness-aware aggregation with local training defenses when graph structure may be corrupted.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these strategies generalize beyond the reported topological-corruption setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the topological corruption models or corruption rates.
The abstract does not identify datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not provide theoretical guarantees or details of the aggregation and local-enhancement procedures.
